lesson: For capital-intensive AI/semiconductor companies, pull segment-level revenue breakdowns to substantiate or refute customer/product concentration risk claims, not just generic 10-K risk-factor language
When a stock move is attributed to 'raised guidance,' capture the actual guidance numbers (old vs new, consensus vs actual) alongside the price reaction for a verifiable causal link

Always reconcile conflicting leverage/valuation metrics (e.g., balance-sheet debt/equity vs TTM debt/equity) before including both in a brief — pick one with a stated methodology or clearly label the gap as unresolved
For high-beta growth stocks, pair volatility/beta stats with analyst consensus price targets and peer multiples so 'premium valuation' claims have relative, not just historical, context
Treat insider sales as directional signals only after checking filing type (10b5-1 scheduled vs discretionary) — undifferentiated insider-sale mentions overstate bearish signal strength
For AI/semiconductor dominance claims, always pull peer/competitor market share or revenue growth comparisons (AMD, custom ASICs) rather than asserting dominance from one company's data alone
For companies with disclosed customer concentration risk, extract the specific percentage (e.g., '% of revenue from top 2 customers') from filings instead of only quoting qualitative risk language
When citing beta or volatility metrics from multiple tools, cross-check for consistency and reconcile discrepancies before publishing
For high-growth/high-multiple tech names, pull analyst consensus price targets and EPS revision trends to substantiate or challenge 'reasonable valuation' claims
For export-control-sensitive companies, quantify exposure (e.g., % of revenue from restricted markets) rather than relying solely on risk-factor boilerplate
